text:
Sam: Heads up — CI batch-sampler alert just flagged a regression after the kernel router tweak. p99 up ~12% on xlarge kernels, KV hit rate dropped for replayed-concat traffic. Opening a triage thread.

Anya: Ugh. I saw a faint blip in the nightly graphs but ignored it. Do you have the replay vs synthetic split? :eyes:

Sam: Quick numbers from the nightly run:```
Model: gpt-medium-8k
kernel: kernel-v4-routerA
batch_sampler: adaptive-0.8
p50: 12ms
p95: 45ms
p99: 128ms -> 143ms (+12%)
kv_hit: 0.82 -> 0.61
```

Matt: That kv_hit drop is suspicious — could be a change in prefix matching or the new router preferring cold paths. Did we change the cache selector threshold?

Riley: I pushed a router tweak yesterday that biases short sequences toward kernel-v4 to reduce cold-start overhead. Might be interacting with our replay harness (longer concatenated prompts).

Anya: Can we repro locally with the replay harness and the same sampling? What command did CI run?

Sam: CI command I used: `./ci/run_bench --profile nightly --traffic replay --seed 2026 --kernel kernel-v4-routerA --sampler adaptive:0.8`

QA: I can run a sampled synthetic job with `--traffic sampled` and the same seed. I'll run both and post quick diffs.

CI Bot: nightly-bench[1869001200]: job finished. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/1869001200/nightly-bench.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

InfraBot: Dashboard snapshot: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/eng-runtime/1869001234 — kv_hit decline and p99 spike pinned between 02:10-02:17 UTC.

Matt: If kernel router is preferring kernel-v4 for short sequences, and replayed traffic has longer concatenated prefixes, we could be suffering suboptimal kernel selection mid-request (router switches after initial tokens). That would evict KV entries or force recompile paths.

Anya: Good point. Could be KV cache churn. Let's check kvcache eviction rate in the profiler. Sam, can you dump the `kvcache.metrics` we log in the harness?

Sam: Pasted the metrics tail from the artifact:```
kvcache.evictions: 312 -> 892
kvcache.load_time_ms: 4.1 -> 9.8
active_kv_sessions: 48 -> 62
```

Riley: Wow — evictions tripled. That explains kv_hit drop. Two hypotheses: router change increases cold-path routing causing additional distinct cache keys, or batching heuristic changed effective working set.

Matt: To isolate, we should: 1) run the same replay with kernel-v3 router, 2) run synthetic sampled traffic with v4, and 3) run with kv-warmup enabled. Quick triage matrix.

Anya: I'll run 1 & 2 in parallel. Commands:```
# compare routers
./tools/replay --seed 2026 --traffic replay --kernel kernel-v3-routerB --out /tmp/res_v3
./tools/replay --seed 2026 --traffic sampled --kernel kernel-v4-routerA --out /tmp/res_v4
# kv warmup toggle
./tools/replay --seed 2026 --traffic replay --kernel kernel-v4-routerA --kv-warmup 0.9 --out /tmp/res_warm
```

QA: ETA ~12m. Will post trimmed logs and p99 numbers.

Sam: If kv-warmup reduces p99 back to baseline, we can attribute to warmup/eviction behaviour and roll a patch to the router to prewarm or avoid mid-request kernel switches.

CI Bot: sanity-check: nightly threshold for p99 is 20% relative. Current is below threshold but the kv_hit shift could indicate future flaps. Marking flaky-alert for human triage.

Riley: Also worth checking batching footprints — the sampler bias in adaptive-0.8 increases micro-batch variance; higher variance can increase memory pressure on kvcache. I have a quick patch to clamp sampler variance.

Matt: Good. After Anya's runs, let's do a small controlled loadtest with `--concurrency 64` to surface any memory pressure. If that reproduces, we can A/B the sampler clamp.

Anya: Results: v3 replay p99=129ms (baseline), v4 sampled p99=142ms (regression), v4 replay+kv-warmup p99=131ms. Evictions: v3=328, v4=890, v4+warmup=356. Quick takeaway: warmup mitigates a lot.

Sam: Nice reproducer. Action items: 1) Riley to prototype sampler clamp + fallback to avoid inter-kernel switches mid-request (PR by EOD). 2) Riley/Infra to add kvcache eviction metric alerts in CI (threshold 500/hr). 3) Anya/QA add a synthetic sampled job to nightly matrix to catch sampler-induced variance. 4) Matt to run a 1-hour soak with concurrency 64 to watch long tail.

Riley: I'll open the PR and include a small unit test in the sampler harness.

QA: I'll add the sampled job to nightly and enable artifact retention for 48h.

Sam: Thanks everyone. If PR fixes latency, we can avoid reverting router change. Marking follow-ups in the sprint. :thumbsup:
